candidate.name: Kalari chikitsa (Kalari marma and traditional Kalari healing)
candidate.reason: The traditional Kalari healing arts (marma chikitsa, uzhichil, chavutti thirumal) form an active, visitable therapeutic‑cultural tradition closely linked with Kalaripayattu training centres across Kerala.

claims.claim: Kerala Tourism describes marmashastra (marma science) as part of Shalyatantra and notes its role in Kalaripayattu training.
Kerala Tourism and practitioner materials describe marma mapping and marmavidya as central elements taught alongside Kalari training.
Common Kalari therapies include thaila lepanam (oil application), kai uzhichil (hand oil massage) and chavutti/chavutti thirumal (rope‑supported foot massage).
Many active kalari schools and clinics in Kerala advertise marma/kalari treatment and residential therapeutic programmes (example providers: Kalarigram, Athma Kalari, Dhanurveda Kovalam, ENS Kalari).
A DST / IndiaScience project listing names a 2024–2027 project to develop a Kalari‑Vedic treatment protocol and research centres for stroke rehabilitation (implementing agency named).

Contemporary clinical and observational research engages with traditional oil and massage therapies in neurological rehabilitation (example: PMC article on Ayurvedic massage in post‑stroke patients, 2019).

Safety note: marma manipulations and chavutti can be forceful and should be performed only by experienced practitioners; obtain medical clearance for fractures, bleeding disorders, pregnancy and major cardiovascular disease before treatment.
National emergency number in India is 112 (Emergency Response Support System); travellers are advised to use it for police, ambulance and fire emergencies.

results.evidence: Details 108/107 marmas by tradition and region, names/consequences, and explicit teaching of Marmavidya alongside training with strict limits.

results.claim: Common Kalari therapies include thaila lepanam (oil application), kai uzhichil (hand oil massage) and chavutti/chavutti thirumal (rope-supported foot massage).
results.evidence: Dedicated sections on Thaila Lepanam, Kai Uzhichil (with dosha variations), and Chavitti Uzhichil (rope-supported foot massage by experienced asan).

results.claim: Many active kalari schools and clinics in Kerala advertise marma/kalari treatment and residential therapeutic programmes (example providers: Kalarigram, Athma Kalari, Dhanurveda Kovalam, ENS Kalari).
results.evidence: Kalarigram page confirms active Kalari Marma Chikitsa services for injuries, rehab and stroke recovery; does not list the other named providers.
results.fix: Remove or separately verify the specific example providers beyond Kalarigram.

results.claim: A DST / IndiaScience project listing names a 2024–2027 project to develop a Kalari-Vedic treatment protocol and research centres for stroke rehabilitation (implementing agency named).
results.evidence: Exact project title, 2024–2027 timeline, PI Dr. Vivek Nambiar (Amrita), implementing agency Amrita Institute of Medical Science, focus on Kalari-Vedic protocol and centres for stroke recovery.

results.claim: Contemporary clinical and observational research engages with traditional oil and massage therapies in neurological rehabilitation (example: PMC article on Ayurvedic massage in post-stroke patients, 2019).
results.evidence: 2018/2019 prospective study on Ayurvedic massage (Abhyanga + steam) as adjunct to PT in post-stroke patients for flaccidity, spasticity and locomotion outcomes.

results.claim: Safety note: marma manipulations and chavutti can be forceful and should be performed only by experienced practitioners; obtain medical clearance for fractures, bleeding disorders, pregnancy and major cardiovascular disease before treatment.
results.evidence: Protocol page states marma treatment is potentially dangerous, only disciplined students should learn it, and attacking marmas should be used only in life-threatening situations.
results.fix: Revise safety checklist to match source wording or cite an additional clinical/medical source for the specific contraindications listed.
